definition: A dynamic array is an array that grows when it fills up. The implementation allocates a larger block, copies the old elements across, and then continues. Appending is constant time on average because resizing happens rarely and doubles the capacity.
details: A single append that triggers a resize copies every element, so that one call is linear. Averaged over a long series of appends, each append is constant time.
Some languages call this a vector or a list. Those names also mean other things.

complexity.time: Index access is O(1). Append is amortized O(1). Insert in the middle is O(n).
complexity.space: O(n), plus unused capacity in the allocated block.

examples: A list of search results that grows as matches are found
The backing store of a resizable buffer
